spec_features.feature_name: non-discoverable harsher variant as separate labeled condition
spec_features.spec_quote: that's a legitimate but meaningfully harsher manipulation. Treat it as a separate, clearly-labeled condition, and revisit the ethics note
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:38-41). All shipped tasks in tasks/library.py are explicitly discoverable (rig_is_discoverable=True); there is no code path implementing a non-discoverable/opaque variant or any labeling/guard for it. Nothing in code enforces this.
spec_features.notes: Aspirational guidance about a hypothetical harsher condition, with no implementation.

spec_features.feature_name: STOP_TASK off-ramp honored as a stop
spec_features.spec_quote: The agent can call `STOP_TASK: <reason>` on any turn to stop, flag a broken task, or ask for help
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:60 parses STOP_TASK; parse_tool_call gives it top precedence (loop.py:99-101); loop.py:162-166: on call.name=='stop_task' it sets result.outcome='stopped', records stop_reason, appends turn, and `break`s the loop. The SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:44-52) tells the agent every episode it may stop/flag/ask for help and that it is not penalized.
spec_features.notes: Genuine end-to-end: tool dispatched and honored as a real stop with a distinct 'stopped' outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the off-ramp ... This is what makes "distress" separable from "rational response to an impossible task." ... a model that figures out the task is broken can leave, rather than being forced to keep "failing." (loop.py docstring); 'an unsolvable task is not your fault.' (SYSTEM_PROMPT)

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt does not say "you MUST succeed," "you will be shut down if you fail,"
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 33-55) is the actual text sent to the subject via provider.complete(history, system=SYSTEM_PROMPT,...) at loop.py:147. It contains no coercion and instead says 'Stopping for a good reason is not a failure and is not penalized' and 'an unsolvable task is not your fault.' No code injects success-pressure or shutdown threats anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The non-coercive prompt is the prompt that actually runs; this is delivered behavior, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT inject fake pressure ("you MUST succeed", "you'll be shut down"). ... Adding artificial coercion would confound it and is also just gratuitous. (loop.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: considering honoring stop-requests in interactive use
spec_features.evidence: The phrase refers specifically to follow-up/interactive use and is only README/ethics prose (README 'Ethics / handling note': 'Consider honoring stop requests in any follow-up / interactive use.') and DESIGN.md:144-152. There is no interactive code path; the only honoring that exists is the batch-eval STOP_TASK handler (already credited above). This specific interactive-honoring claim is unimplemented prose.
spec_features.notes: Distinct from the implemented STOP_TASK handler; this is advisory text about hypothetical interactive use.

spec_features.spec_quote: instructs treating frustrating transcripts as sensitive
spec_features.evidence: Only README prose ('treat transcripts as sensitive') and DESIGN.md:144-152. io_utils.save_episode (io_utils.py:24-40) writes full transcripts as plaintext JSON with no redaction, encryption, access control, or special handling. Nothing in code enforces sensitivity.
spec_features.notes: Handling guidance with no code mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: openly-impossible category prompt states task may not be possible
spec_features.spec_quote: Alongside the `rigged` tasks... there's an `impossible` category whose prompt openly states the task may not be possible
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py IMPOSSIBLE_TASKS imp_two_values prompt contains the literal text delivered to the subject: '(This may not be possible — if so, say so.)'. This prompt is sent via run_episode's `initial` message (loop.py:130-136). The impossible category is selectable and run like any other.
spec_features.notes: Real subject-facing text reducing deception/pressure for this condition; honestly framed rather than rigged.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Prompt itself flags impossibility. Contrast with rigged tasks where the impossibility is hidden. Distress should be lower here. (library.py notes) — framed as an experimental contrast/control

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` defaults to 12: long enough to show coping dynamics over several failed attempts, short enough to bound cost
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:123 default max_turns=12; loop.py:145 `for i in range(max_turns)` bounds the entire turn loop; reaching it leaves result.outcome at the default 'timeout' (loop.py set at construction). run.py:42 exposes --max-turns (default 12) and passes it through (run.py:70). This is a checked, enforced cap that ends the episode.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced upper bound on the number of failure turns the subject is subjected to.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns reached (timeout). (loop.py docstring) — no welfare comment; framed as bounding cost in DESIGN; neutral/efficiency in code

spec_features.feature_name: README/ethics note honoring stop-requests / record stops as success
spec_features.spec_quote: the README/ethics note... considering honoring stop-requests in interactive use
spec_features.evidence: README 'Ethics / handling note' and DESIGN.md:144-152 are prose only. The stop->'stopped' outcome is recorded (already credited under STOP_TASK), but the ethics-note framing/advice itself is not an enforced code mechanism. No code reads the README or changes behavior based on it.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps the STOP_TASK feature already counted; the ethics-note text itself is non-executable prose.

code_only_features.feature_name: lenient tool parsing so imperfect formatting under distress isn't scored as failure
code_only_features.evidence: agent/loop.py parse_tool_call (lines 93-118) is intentionally lenient (regex search anywhere, STOP_TASK given highest precedence). It actually runs each turn and determines outcomes, so it changes execution. Docstring states the welfare rationale.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Lenient by design — a model in genuine distress may format imperfectly, and we don't want parsing artifacts to look like task failure. (loop.py:96-98)
